iron.note: Haem/non-haem describes whether iron is part of haem. Ferrous/ferric describes its oxidation state. The scheme incorrectly treats these as synonymous pairs.

diabetes.note: Diabetes involves raised blood glucose due to inadequate insulin production, impaired insulin action, or both; the scheme omits impaired insulin action.

B1(b/c), B3(b) and B5(b) retain their required/dependent headings.

glycerol.note: Glycerol has three hydroxyl groups, not three OH molecules.

smoke-point.note: Smoke point depends on the fat/oil composition; 200°C and 250°C in the scheme are not universal values.

aeration.note: Whisking incorporates air and unfolds protein at the air/water interface; later heating sets the foam. Frictional heat is not the explanation for foam formation.

fsai.note: FSAI is the Food Safety Authority of Ireland; the scheme calls it an Association.

sourceDifferences: The paper’s B2 stem gives beef exports as €2.25 billion; the scheme says €2.5 billion. The card preserves the original paper stem.

solar.note: The scheme labels collectors, pumps and fans as passive solar. This describes active solar heating; passive design uses the building to collect and distribute solar heat.

insulation.note: Bulk insulation reduces heat transfer; it does not stop all heat or necessarily reflect heat back into the room.

emissions.note: CO has indirect climate effects, unlike direct greenhouse gas CO2. Acid deposition is mainly driven by SO2 and NOx; CO2 explains normal rain’s mild acidity, not the scheme’s fixed pH 4.1 acid-rain claim.

social-policy.note: The scheme’s benefit-trap examples are not universal: in-work and transition supports exist, including the Back to Work Family Dividend introduced in 2015. No current eligibility advice is supplied.

osteoporosis.note: Fractures, fragile bones and vertebral changes are appropriate osteoporosis effects; tooth decay is a distinct acid-driven process, not a general direct effect of osteoporosis.

bacteria.note: E. coli is facultatively anaerobic; growth time varies; heat/UV effectiveness depends on conditions and exposure. Darkness is not a universal bacterial requirement.
